name: cardgame-winning-losing-conditions-rules
title: Winning & Losing Conditions Rules (Amaranth Expanse rules — game-end conditions)
pitch: Extend design/rules.md with the one foundational rules gap none of the eleven queued cardgame units cover: how a player actually loses and a game actually ends.
why_now: The shipped Spatial Battlefield section (Section 8) already defines Homeworld Capture, and in-flight units (core-rules, card-types-templating, spatial-map-setup) build turn structure, resources, templating, and map setup on top of it — but no document anywhere states what capturing a Homeworld does to the game, or how a game concludes. Per T1, MVP means full decided scope; shipping cards and a playtest procedure without a win/loss rule leaves the design phase one load-bearing gap short of playable.
expected_outcome: design/rules.md contains a new numbered 'Winning & Losing Conditions' section stating the elimination condition tied to Section 8's Capture rule (by cross-reference, not restatement), plus a worked example resolving a concrete game-end edge case.
intent: Fifth-plus design deliverable for the cardGame pilot: design/rules.md establishes Turn Structure, Resources, Priority & Timing, Zones, and (Section 8) the Spatial Battlefield's Capture mechanic, but no section anywhere states what happens when a Homeworld is captured or how a game ends. This unit adds a Winning & Losing Conditions section defining player elimination and game-end conditions, cross-referencing Section 8's existing Capture rule rather than redefining it, at the MTG-Comprehensive-Rules structural bar (T9) — numbered subsection, glossary-first terms, at least one worked edge-case example. Pure design/rules text; no code, no game software (T8).

criteria.text: design/rules.md gains a new numbered 'Winning & Losing Conditions' section defining at least one player-elimination condition, tied explicitly to the Homeworld Capture rule already defined in Section 8 by cross-referencing its section number rather than restating the mechanic
The section states what ends the game (a single remaining un-eliminated player, or an explicit draw condition) and how remaining players' turns proceed once another player is eliminated

The section includes at least one numbered worked example resolving a concrete game-end edge case (e.g. two players eliminated in the same turn), matching the MTG-Comprehensive-Rules-level rigor bar (T9) used by the shipped Spatial Battlefield section
New terms introduced by this section (e.g. 'eliminated', 'game end') are added to the Section 2 glossary before substantive use, consistent with rules.md's existing glossary-first discipline
The new section does not redefine or contradict the existing Section 8 Capture rule — it only adds the game-end consequence of capture, cross-referencing rather than restating the mechanic
